newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - N Brown current sales up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - N Brown current sales up 15 pct.

text.p: British direct mail order retailer N Brown Group Plc said on Tuesday that sales in the first six weeks of the current year were up by around 15 percent and the pace of growth was likely to be maintained.
N Brown, which has abandoned talks to buy Sears Plc's Freemans business, said pretax profits rose 19 percent in the year to March 1 and sales grew 21.5 percent.

"It was a remarkable result...If you take into account the previous year's 53-week period and a value-added-tax windfall, then that puts the earnings rise at about 25 percent," chief executive Jim Martin said in a telephone interview.
Martin said around three percent profit growth came from newly-acquired Sartor, a household products and inexpensive clothing retailer, and the remainder was organic.
He said it would be difficult to maintain that level of profit growth, which was driven by higher customer recruitment and wider womenswear, menswear and furniture ranges.
"But we had 15 percent sales growth in the first six weeks and that level is certainly possible for the future," Martin said, adding that margins remained constant.
He said N Brown was maintaining its share -- around 25 percent -- of the direct home shopping market in which it competes with Next Plc, among others.
The company has around five percent of the wider home shopping market, which includes agency companies such as Great Universal Stores Plc and Littlewoods.

Martin said his Manchester-based company was "not too worried" about Littlewoods' move to buy Freemans. Retail industry sources believe Littlewoods will overcome competition watchdog concerns and take over the Sears' subsidiary, Britain's third-largest mail order company.
"We feel we have our own part of the marketplace and we are quite satisfied with that," he said.
Martin said N Brown was increasingly targeting older consumers, between 30 and retirement age, who were benefitting from higher savings, better pensions and inheritance windfalls.

"The post-war baby boomers will be coming of age in the late 90s and in early 2000s and there will be a 27 percent increase in the next 10 years in women between 55 and 64," he said, adding that N Brown would also seek to cater for low-income groups.

N Brown figures show sales from its midlife catalogue ranges, including J D Williams, Shoe Tailor, Oxendales and Fifty Plus, rose 14 percent last year, accounting for 205 million stg of total catalogue sales of 274 million.
Sales to the elderly soared over 100 percent to 17 million.
